valid.jsonl.about: A complete signed chain. The second model call records only what changed.

redacted.jsonl.about: Every redactable value removed with its salt. Still verifies.

edited-content.jsonl.about: A tool result edited after the fact, its digest left as it was.

edited-record.jsonl.about: An approval rewritten to blame a person, record_hash left as it was.

rewritten-chain.jsonl.about: The same edit with every hash recomputed: the signed Merkle root no longer matches, and the signature no longer covers the new link.

deleted-record.jsonl.about: The tool call that sent the email removed.

bad-context-base.jsonl.about: A model call that points back to a record that is not a model call. Signed, so only the base is wrong.

missing-salt.jsonl.about: A 1.0 value with an unsalted digest, which could be guessed.

other-key.jsonl.about: A consistent chain signed by a key that is not pinned.

newer-minor.jsonl.about: Written by a later minor version (1.1) with a field 1.0 doesn't know. Verifies, with the field reported as not checked.

malformed-salt.jsonl.about: A salt that is not base64 in its one canonical spelling: a spare bit of its last letter is set. No hash covers a salt, so nothing else shows it.

crlf-line-ends.jsonl.about: Every line ended by CR LF. A carriage return directly before the line end is part of the line end.

blank-line.jsonl.about: An empty line between two records. A blank line is refused, not skipped.

lone-cr.jsonl.about: One carriage return inside the record at seq 4, after its first comma. JSON reads it as white space, and a reader that ends lines at CR sees two lines. The line is refused, so the record is missing from the chain.

incomplete-last-line.jsonl.about: The valid chain, then 59 bytes of a next record with no line end, as a write that was cut leaves them. Bytes after the last LF that are not a closed JSON object are not a record: they are not read, and the verdict is for the complete lines.

no-final-line-feed.jsonl.about: The valid chain without the LF that ends its last line, the checkpoint. The bytes after the last LF are a closed JSON object, a whole record, so they are read as the last line like any other, with a warning that the line end is missing.

integer-with-fraction.jsonl.about: step_id of the record at seq 1 written 1.0. An integer field is written without a fraction or an exponent, in every field the schema types as an integer.

integer-minus-zero.jsonl.about: seq of the first record written -0. Zero has one spelling in an integer field, 0.

large-numbers.jsonl.about: Whole numbers past 2^53 - 1 in a record, written as canonical JSON writes them: 9007199254740992 and 9223372036854776000.

respelled-integer.jsonl.about: The same file with 9007199254740992 written 9007199254740993. Both read as the same double, so every hash still matches, and a reader with exact integers sees another number. Past 2^53 - 1 only the canonical spelling is accepted: the line is refused, so the record at seq 5 is missing from the chain.

nesting-128.jsonl.about: A value nested 128 levels deep, the deepest that is read: the record is level 1, its attributes level 2, and 126 arrays inside each other follow.

nesting-129.jsonl.about: The same with one array more, 129 levels. The line is refused, so the record at seq 5 is missing from the chain.

worked_example.rule: record_hash = sha256(JCS(record without record_hash, without every redactable value and salt))
